items.claim: `pathToAnchors` reused a quadratic's control point as both cubic handles, so editing any anchor bulged the path's `Q` segments
items.note: It now converts each quadratic to the cubic that traces the same curve. `heldBy` reads the quadratics without converting them, so both handles still map to the control point (`[0, 1, 1, 2]` still holds).

items.claim: `offsetCornerTraces` read a convex `square` corner as concave, so its trace moved inward and the offset lost the corner
items.note: It now tests convexity against the outline with every corner left sharp, which works for any corner shape. Added tests for convex and concave corners.

items.claim: `isAnchorSmooth` counted two handles pointing the same way as smooth, so fairing, handle drags and bends altered cusps
items.note: It now also requires the handles to point opposite ways (negative dot product).

items.claim: `growRegion`'s round join bent a U-turn cap back into the shape, depending on which way rounding tipped a near-zero cross product
items.note: A U-turn's arc now always turns outward.

items.claim: `growRegion` used one winding sign for the whole path, so a separate shape wound the other way shrank instead of growing
items.note: Each contour now finds its outside by testing the winding number on both sides of it (new `contourSides.ts`). If neither side or both sides are unfilled, it falls back to the path's sign. Holes still shrink.

items.claim: `flatAnchorIndices` started a subpath opened without an `M` at the wrong point, so every later anchor's index was one too high
items.note: It now starts that subpath at the pen position. A closing curve that folds onto that uncounted start reads -1, and `carryCorners` and `restoreCorners` skip it.
